input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: Section 13.1 creates a very long term (running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term on a Product-by-Product/country-by-country basis). Array has no termination-for-convenience right at all (its exits under 13.3, 13.4 and 8.2 are for breach, insolvency or competing-product breach), so the vendor-side prong of the rule is satisfied. However, our at-will exit under Section 13.2 does not exist until the later of a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of each of the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, i.e. we are locked in for the entire development and pre-launch phase of a multi-year term with no convenience exit (only the narrow Safety/Efficacy Reasons rights in 13.5). That fails the fallback on a material term (existence of a customer convenience right during the term) and sits in walk-away territory. The redline removes the commencement trigger so we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice — the fallback notice period rather than the preferred 30 days, which is proportionate here given the transition mechanics in Article XIV. Noted but not separately flagged: the notice period in 13.2 is redacted and should be confirmed at 30–90 days; the wind-down/transfer costs allocated to Ono under 14.2(a) and the post-termination Competing Product restriction in Section 8.2 operate as economic consequences of an at-will exit and should be reviewed under the pricing/exclusivity rules rather than double-flagged here.

proposal.summary: Make Ono's at-will termination right available from the Effective Date on 90 days' notice, rather than only after first commercial sale of both Products.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the trigger that delays our at-will exit until after First Commercial Sale of both Products, so we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice; our playbook requires a customer convenience right throughout a multi-year term (preferred 30 days' notice), and we are accepting the longer 90-day notice period as a fallback in recognition of Array's transition planning.
